description: Stephen Nover review, checked 19 Nov 2026: prices on five sites from $25 to $1,999, the credit guarantees, his NFL claims checked and what bettors said.
dek: A former Las Vegas Review-Journal gaming writer, UNLV instructor and VegasInsider veteran who has sold picks since the late 1990s. The same picks are sold on at least five sites at different prices, from $25 a game to $1,999 a year. The store records we checked are modest over large samples, and the same NFL season is shown four different ways depending on the site.

short_answer: Stephen Nover is a long standing Las Vegas name. The seller bios say he covered sports gaming for the Las Vegas Review-Journal from 1984 to 1997, wrote three books including Winning Fantasy Football, taught a football handicapping class at UNLV and co hosted the Stardust Line radio show in the 1990s. TheRX members in 2003 described him as one of the people who started VegasInsider. He still writes picks for VegasInsider and sells them on PickDawgz, StatSalt and the SportsCapping network.

The best numbers we could check are the SportsCapping streaks: 456-390 for all sports since 12 Sep 2025, which is 53.9% and $2,087 at $100 a play, about +2.5% on 846 plays, and 87-63 in the NFL since 5 Jan 2025. Those are winning but small. The marketing lines are harder to square: on 19 Nov 2026 his current NFL season was shown as 27-17-1 on SportsCapping sites, 26-15-1 on StatSalt, 12-7-1 and 10-6 on PickDawgz, and 9-5 on a StatSalt badge. His NFL history is given as 29 of 34, 26 of 30, 24 of 27 and 21 of 23 winning seasons.

Independent buyer posts are few. A store owned review site shows a 3.90 out of 5 rating from 42 votes with four short positive comments about his basketball picks. TheRX members repost his CFL plays and in 2025 noted his CFL season record. We found no complaint threads, no refund disputes and no news coverage of problems.

guarantee: On the SportsCapping network (SportsCapping, CappersPicks, Capper Reviews, Boyd's Bets) the written policy says: "if you don’t show a profit during your paid subscription period, you’ll receive an equal-length subscription free of charge." It adds "We do not offer monetary refunds", grades "All plays" on "a 100-unit flat betting system", allows "Only one free subscription" per purchase and states "There is no profit guarantee on season-long subscriptions." The CappersPicks 7-Day NFL listing words it as "GUARANTEED TO WIN or you get another 7 days FREE!"

On PickDawgz the banner says "Credit guarantee on applicable packages. If it doesn't profit, you get a full credit. Automatically." The credit is issued "after picks are graded and verified" and "Credits expire 9 months after they are added to your account." On 19 Nov 2026 only the two $25 Thursday picks were marked as guaranteed; the passes were not.
StatSalt and the VI Premium plan page showed no guarantee wording. No site we read refunds cash, and none covers what you lose on the bets themselves.

claims_note: The career claims also drift. The bios say professional handicapper since 1999, active since 1997, "more than 25 years", "30 years", "nearly 50 years" and "60 years worth of sports experience". Some of these may count his writing years, but none of the pages says so.

PickDawgz shows its own windows that do not add up: +549 units for the last 30 days but +530 for the last 12 months, while its league table sums to +1,140. We could not tell which window the table uses.
record: What is independently logged: nothing we could find that covers his paid picks across all the sites that sell them. TheRX members repost some of his plays, and in August 2025 one member noted his CFL season at 15-8 and then 16-8, but no outside site keeps a full ledger.

What the stores publish: SportsCapping shows streaks and about 44 leaderboard finishes, including #1 in basketball in 2019-2020 at 176-113 (60.9%, $5,191) and in 2014-2015 at 182-127 (58.9%, $4,235). PickDawgz showed 13-5 in the NBA, 10-6 in the NFL and 3-2 in college basketball, and a first page of picks from 15 to 18 Nov 2026 at 6 wins and 4 losses. StatSalt showed three wins and two losses from 16 to 18 Nov 2026. VegasInsider lists leaderboard finishes from 2020-21 to 2022-23 only.

Each store sells his picks and grades them itself, and the stores do not agree on the same season. The long run SportsCapping figure, 53.9% over 846 plays, is the most useful number we found, and it is a small winning edge rather than the 60% plus the headlines suggest.

our_data.text: In this edition no Stephen Nover pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how he performs.

customers_intro: We found few posts by buyers. The comments we could open sit on a review site that is part of the network selling his picks, plus TheRX forum posts from 2003 and 2025. No complaint threads turned up.

customers.text: We found about ten posts that mention Stephen Nover as a pick seller, on two sites, from 2003 to 2026. The most direct are four undated comments on Capper Reviews, a site that says it belongs to the SportsCapping network selling his picks: all four praise his basketball knowledge, one says a March basketball subscription was going well, and the site shows 3.90 out of 5 from 42 votes. On TheRX in 2003 members hoped he would return to make picks when VegasInsider changed hands, and in 2025 a member reposting his CFL plays tracked his CFL season at 15-8 and 16-8 and said another well known tout copies his CFL picks. One older affiliate review notes his first losing NFL year after fifteen winning ones. We found no complaints about billing, refunds or missing picks, and no independent post confirming his headline records.

Four comments on Capper Reviews: one buyer said they bought a basketball subscription in March and was pleased so far; others called his college and pro basketball plays consistently solid, said they had followed him on other sites, and planned to buy if his college basketball start went well. The site states that Nover "sells picks through the SportsCapping network, which Capper Reviews is part of."
A TheRX member posting Nover's CFL play for the weekend noted his CFL season picks were 15-8, and added that another paid handicapper copies some of the same picks but was 8-9.
The next day the same thread updated his CFL season to 16-8 and repeated that the other handicapper usually copies his CFL picks. We did not verify either record.
In a TheRX thread about the sale of VegasInsider, a member said they hoped the site's original founders would bring Nover back to make picks.
Replies in the same thread said Nover and another man had originally started VegasInsider, and doubted whether he would join the founders' new venture.
TheRX's October 2026 service play rules list many services whose plays members may not post; Nover and VegasInsider are not on that list, and members still repost his plays.

We found no BBB profile, no app store listing, no news coverage of complaints and no CapperTek reviews for Nover. The affiliate review on RideTheHotHand had no visible comments. Our Reddit library, harvested from r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting through the Arctic Shift archive, holds no buyer post about him; live full text searches of the archive timed out. A Pregame forum thread about him refused automated access, so we left it out.

conflicts: SportsCapping (Boyd Information Group) sells his picks and grades them. CappersPicks, Capper Reviews and Boyd's Bets show the same packages, and Capper Reviews says it is part of the SportsCapping network, so review pages on those sites come from the seller's own sales channel.
VegasInsider lists him as one of its experts, sells his picks inside VI Premium and publishes his leaderboard finishes, which it says it tracks itself.
RideTheHotHand states that it is compensated by some of the services its handicappers work with, and its link to his picks carries a partner ID.
strengths: A long and public career under his own name: newspaper gaming writer, author, UNLV instructor and VegasInsider expert.
The largest store record we found, 456-390 since 12 Sep 2025, is a winning mark over a big sample, even if a small one.
Stores show losses as well as wins, including a 5-9 figure on his all sports subscriptions this season.
Cheap ways to try him: $25 single picks, some with automatic credit if they lose, and $49 three day passes on StatSalt.
No complaint threads, refund disputes or news stories against him turned up in our search.
concerns: The same NFL season is shown as 27-17-1, 26-15-1, 12-7-1, 10-6 and 9-5 on different sites on the same day.
Career claims conflict: 29 of 34, 26 of 30, 24 of 27 and 21 of 23 winning NFL seasons; since 1997 or 1999; 25, 30 or nearly 50 years.
The "No. 1 NFL capper in 2012 cashing 69 percent" line does not match the network's own 2012 record of 68-34 (66.7%).
Every record is graded by a site that sells his picks; no outside ledger covers his paid plays.

The same package costs different amounts on different sites (a year of all sports is $1,990 or $1,999; the NFL season $250 or $349.95), and guarantees differ too, with nothing on season passes and no cash refunds anywhere.
checklist: Compare the price and guarantee on SportsCapping, CappersPicks, PickDawgz and StatSalt before you buy; they differ for the same picks.
Ask the seller which record covers the picks you will actually receive, and for the full log from a fixed date.
Treat a single season headline as marketing until you see the game by game list behind it.
Count units, not wins: 54% over 846 plays at $100 a play earned about $2,087.
Remember that season passes carry no guarantee on the SportsCapping network, and credits on PickDawgz expire after 9 months.
Log each pick with the line and time you received it, and compare after a month.
faq: He is a real, long standing Las Vegas handicapper and former Review-Journal gaming writer who still writes for VegasInsider and sells picks on several sites. Whether his picks win over time is not independently shown; each store grades its own record, and the stores do not agree with each other.
How much does Stephen Nover cost?

On 19 Nov 2026 single picks were $25, StatSalt three day passes $49, SportsCapping network day passes $69.95 to $79.95, 7 days $199.95, 30 days $399.95 and a year $1,990. PickDawgz charged $99 for 3 days, $175 for 7, $350 for 30 and $1,999 for a year.
Does Stephen Nover have a verified record?
No. SportsCapping shows 456-390 for all sports since 12 Sep 2025, about 53.9%, graded by itself. VegasInsider lists leaderboard finishes through 2022-23. No independent log covers his paid picks.
What is the guarantee on Stephen Nover's picks?

It depends on the site. SportsCapping network sites give one free subscription of the same length after a losing term, no cash refunds and nothing on season passes. PickDawgz gives an automatic credit, valid 9 months, only on packages marked as guaranteed.
Why are there different NFL records for him?

Each site seems to track a different set of his plays from a different start. On 19 Nov 2026 we saw 27-17-1, 26-15-1, 12-7-1, 10-6 and 9-5 for the current NFL season. Ask the site you buy from which plays its number counts.

He has a real track record in the industry and his biggest store sample is a small winning one. But the edge shown is about 2.5% on all sports plays, the marketing figures conflict, and nothing independent proves he beats 52.4% at -110 over time. Start with a single pick and track it yourself.
